The answer is the synapse. A synapse is the specialized junction where one neuron communicates with another — specifically, where the axon terminal of the presynaptic neuron meets the dendrite or cell body of the postsynaptic neuron. Neurotransmitters are released across this tiny gap to transmit electrical signals chemically from one cell to the next, which is how all neural communication occurs throughout your nervous system.
